**Basis for termination of employment (as stated in the employee handbook)**  

| Document & Page | Relevant Text |
|-----------------|----------------|
| *employee_handbook.pdf*, page 4 | “EMPLOYMENT AT THE COMPANY IS ON AN “AT WILL” BASIS AND MAY BE TERMINATED BY THE COMPANY OR THE EMPLOYEE AT ANY TIME FOR ANY REASON.” |
| *employee_handbook.pdf*, page 4 (Hiring Policy) | “Unless otherwise provided in writing, employment with the Company is considered to be at will, so that either party may terminate the relationship at any time and for any lawful reason.” |
| *employee_handbook.pdf*, page 5 | “If the offense is considered serious enough by the supervisor, then the employee may be terminated immediately without warning (i.e. theft or fraud …).” |
| *employee_handbook.pdf*, page 16 | “Your activity can result in disciplinary action up to and including employment termination” (for violations such as undisclosed relationships, false information, defamatory or harassing content, etc.). |

### Summary
- **At‑will employment**: The default rule is that either the Company or the employee may end the employment relationship at any time, for any reason (or for any lawful reason if a written exception exists) [employee_handbook.pdf, p. 4].
- **Immediate termination for serious misconduct**: Certain offenses—specifically theft, fraud, or other serious violations identified by a supervisor—allow the Company to terminate employment immediately without prior warning [employee_handbook.pdf, p. 5].
- **Policy‑based termination**: Violations of company policies (e.g., harassment‑free workplace, improper online conduct, illegal or defamatory content) can also lead to disciplinary action up to termination [employee_handbook.pdf, p. 16].

Thus, your employment can be terminated **at any time for any (lawful) reason under the at‑will doctrine**, and **immediately for serious misconduct such as theft or fraud**, as well as **for breaches of the Company’s conduct policies**.
